title: The winter Europe froze solid ❄️
subject: frost
description:
Could a winter like this happen again? 👇

The Great Frost of 1709 was Europe's coldest winter in 500 years. The Thames and the Baltic Sea froze, wine froze in barrels, and France lost about 600,000 people.

Sources: Britannica (Today in History, January 5: The Great Frost), Wikipedia (Great Frost of 1709; William Derham's measurements, letters of Elizabeth Charlotte, Duchess of Orléans)

scenes.text: People skated through the canals of Venice.
It was January 1709, Europe's coldest winter in 500 years, stretching from England to Russia.
Near London, William Derham measured minus 12 Celsius. The Thames and the Baltic Sea froze.
The Duchess of Orléans wrote: "Never in my life have I seen a winter such as this one."
Wine froze in barrels. Bread had to be cut with an axe. In France, about 600,000 people died.
Scientists still argue whether volcanic ash or a weak Sun caused it.
